newsitem.title: USA: Valujet to resume flights on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Valujet to resume flights on Monday.

text.p: Valuejet Inc said on Thursday that it would resume scheduled operations on Monday between Atlanta and four cities with $19 one-way introductory fares on all non-stop flights.

The airline said it would open its reservations center and begin selling seats Thursday at 1730 EDT, about two hours after the U.S. Department of Transportation gave its final approval for the discount carrier to resume regularly scheduled flights.

Valuejet said the $19 fares would be in effect for flights between September 30 and October 3. Fares would rise to $29 between October 4 and October 15 and to between $29 and $49 from October 16 to October 31. Normal fares would be reinstated on November 1.
Additional flights to 12 more cities would be added in three phases to October 24 when the airline plans to operate 102 daily departures with a fleet of 15 aircraft.

The airline's first four destinations from Atlanta include three Florida cities -- Fort Lauderdale, Orlando and Tampa -- as well as Washington D.C.'s Dulles airport. A system total of 32 peak daily departures will be offered to those cities, ValuJet said.

On October 4, another 18 departures will be added with new non-stop flights to Columbus, Ohio, Newport News/Norfolk, Virginia and New Orleans. Twelve days later, flights will be added to Fort Walton Beach, Fla., Jacksonville, Fla., Louisville, Ky., Memphis, Tenn. and Savannah, Ga.
ValuJet said its final phase of service restoration would begin October 24 with departures between Atlanta and Philadelphia, Raleigh/Durham, N.C., Mobile, Ala., and Chicago's Midway airport.
